claims.text: The initial alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a solid-solution microstructure.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr has poor high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Low-energy Al ion implantation can produce a controlled, thin Al-enriched surface region on as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The implanted near-surface Al will form a continuous and adherent Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
Near-surface Al will oxidize preferentially to form a slow-growing protective Al2O3 layer.
A continuous alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion and suppress oxygen ingress into the alloy bulk.
The surface-localized implantation treatment will not significantly alter the bulk microstructure.
The treatment will significantly improve oxidation resistance relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C in air for approximately 100 hours.
The treated alloy will retain approximately 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
The treated alloy will retain approximately 163–530 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Ion implantation may modify residual stresses or cause localized microstructural changes that influence surface-related mechanical response.
The scalability and uniformity of the implanted enrichment over complex geometries remain uncertain.
Failure to form a continuous adherent alumina scale, to achieve a statistically significant oxidation improvement, or to preserve mechanical properties would falsify the hypothesis.
